summary:
1. What did you develop?
We developed the Airoburn Engineering Command Center, a dual-pillar predictive AI and decision-support platform designed to unified fire safety engineering across space and terrestrial environments.
2. How does it address the challenge?
The platform executes a unique multiphysics technology transfer based on two equally vital pillars:
• The Space Pillar: The system ingests raw NASA PSI microgravity datasets (Heptane, Decane, Dodecane). Our machine learning engine tracks dynamic fuel droplet cores, hot flames, and cool flames to simulate and predict flame behavior in its purest physical state, completely isolated from Earth's gravity-convection factors.
• The Earth Pillar: We transfer these space-calibrated fluid dynamics equations onto a terrestrial Esri GIS map via the Morocco GeoPortal. The platform cross-references vulnerable biomass densities in the Rif region (Chefchaouen, Larache) with active NASA MODIS/VIIRS satellite thermal anomalies and extreme Chergui wind matrices.
3. Why is it important?
This project is critical because it elevates firefighting from reactive containment to predictive science. By providing real-time propagation risk indexes and emergency vocal interfaces, it secures astronaut crews in orbital modules while empowering civil protection units on Earth to deploy Canadair water bombers preemptively, saving vital ecosystems and human lives.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

The Airoburn Engineering Command Center is a unified decision-support dashboard that bridges space engineering and terrestrial wildfire management.

  • Space Module: Our machine learning engine ingests raw NASA microgravity datasets (psi.nasa.gov) to analyze pure combustion kinetics completely isolated from buoyancy-driven convection factors.
  • Earth Module: The platform transfers these space-calibrated fluid dynamics equations into an Esri GIS interface via the Morocco GeoPortal. It cross-references vulnerable biomass densities in the Rif region (Chefchaouen, Larache) with real-time NASA satellite thermal anomalies (MODIS/VIIRS) and extreme Chergui wind matrices to calculate live fire propagation indexes.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Preemption over Reaction: It shifts wildfire fighting into an anticipatory science, evaluating hazards before a fire spirals out of control.
  • Resource Optimization: It empowers civil protection forces to dynamically position and deploy trucks and Canadair water bombers preemptively.
  • Orbital Safety: The system double-functions as a space safety monitor, protecting astronaut crews by identifying invisible microgravity combustion risks (cool flames).

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

The intended impact encompasses environmental, human, and economic scales. By drastically reducing response times for wildfires in Northern Morocco, this platform aims to preserve thousands of hectares of valuable forest ecosystems, achieve a massive reduction in fire-related carbon emissions, and ultimately save human lives among local populations and emergency responders.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • 3D Modeling & CAD: CATIA (Design of reference geometries and structural parameters).
  • Scientific Data Sources: psi.nasa.gov (NASA Physical Sciences Informatics datasets) and Morocco GeoPortal (Esri GIS mapping layers).
  • Development & AI: Python language, Gemini (Advanced code generation and algorithmic logic assistance), and GitHub (Source code version control).
  • Deployment & Cloud Hosting: Streamlit Community Cloud (Application production hosting and public URL deployment).

5. How is your project creative?

Our creativity lies in the multiphysics technology transfer. We pioneered the concept of taking the isolated physics of a micro-flame in space (where buoyancy is zero) and using it to calibrate macro-scale wildfire front kinetics on Earth. Furthermore, the dashboard creatively integrates an AI emergency voice copilot that translates complex telemetry data grids into clear, spoken audio dispatch instructions for operators under extreme crisis stress.

6. What factors did your team consider?

Our team considered critical, real-world environmental and operational variables: the specific biomass density of Moroccan forests, the catastrophic impact of extreme weather conditions (such as the hot Chergui wind and ground temperatures), the real-time availability of satellite feeds, and vital UI/UX accessibility criteria (aerospace dark mode theme) to guarantee instantaneous KPI readability for emergency personnel.
